archetype.name: Game Manager (spot-start backup)
archetype.definition: A veteran undrafted backup who wins only when the run game and defense carry the load. He keeps the ball short and on schedule and has no downfield gear to rescue a game that gets away.

report.headline: Two ugly spot appearances, now QB3: short-area passer with no margin
report.take:
Cooper Rush is what he has been for five seasons: a steady-handed backup whose value depends on the offense around him doing the heavy lifting. In 2026 the Falcons gave him a start in Week 1 and 58% of the snaps in Week 2. Both went badly. He was -15.8 EPA at Pittsburgh and -12.2 against Carolina, and his -0.635 EPA per dropback ranks 42nd of 43 qualifiers. Michael Penix Jr. then took the job, and Rush sits third on the depth chart as of October 13.

The profile explains the results. His intended air yards (5.34) and aggressiveness (7.69%) are tiny. His throws average 5 yards short of the sticks, and Bijan Robinson drew 14 of his 39 targets at -0.475 EPA each. That is a dink-and-check offense, and it collapses when the few throws that do push the ball go wrong. Seven intermediate attempts produced three interceptions and -1.748 EPA per play. On third down he converted 15.4% while facing an average of 8.5 yards to go. His CPOE has been negative every season of his career, so the accuracy deficit is not new. At -13.6 it is just the deepest version of it.

The sample also hides some noise. Five sacks on eight pressures (62.5% pressure-to-sack) runs against his history: he ranked 4th, 11th and 2nd in that stat in 2022, 2024 and 2025, and his offense's line ranks 2nd in hit rate allowed. That number should come down with more snaps. The 10.3% interception rate on 39 attempts will also cool. Still, four interceptions in three Baltimore games last year and four more here suggest turnovers are a real wart once he is asked to throw past the sticks. His best work came working left (83.3% completions, +0.482 EPA) and targeting Drake London (+0.447 per target). Both are small cuts.

Going forward, he is emergency depth. The Falcons are a run-first team: rush EPA ranks 3rd and pass rate over expected ranks 29th. That is the only environment where a Rush start is survivable, and even there the ceiling is a low-volume, low-scoring afternoon.

strengths.title: Historically avoids sacks under pressure
strengths.body: Before this year he converted pressure into sacks at one of the lowest rates among qualifiers, ranking 2nd in 2025 and 4th in 2022. This year's 62.5% comes from just eight pressures, behind a line that ranks 2nd in hit rate allowed. It reads as a blip rather than a new trait.

strengths.title: Functional when working short and left
strengths.body: His short throws (0-9 yards) came in at roughly break-even EPA with a 50% success rate. His throws to the left were efficient. Paired with a run game ranked 3rd in EPA, that is a workable caretaker template on limited volume.

concerns.title: Turnovers whenever he pushes the ball
concerns.body: Three of his four interceptions came on just seven intermediate attempts, and he added a lost fumble. Four interceptions in three games for Baltimore last year say this is not purely a fluke. When he is forced off the checkdown, his accuracy can't hold up the throws.

concerns.title: Chronic below-expected accuracy
concerns.body: His CPOE has been negative every season since 2021, and this year's -13.61 ranks 42nd of 43. His bad-throw rate ranks 37th of 36 charted passers. That is a skill ceiling, not variance, and it caps what any start from him can look like.

concerns.title: Can't move the chains on third down
concerns.body: He converted 15.4% of third downs at an average of 8.5 yards to go, while his throws averaged about five yards short of the sticks. That combination stalls drives and explains the 13- and 3-point outputs in his two games.

trend.note: He went from a -15.8 EPA start in Week 1 to -12.2 EPA on only 58% of snaps in Week 2 (-0.6 fantasy points). He has since slid to QB3 behind a healthy-until-now Penix.

nextGame.headline: QB3 behind Penix; Chicago's stingy short defense fits him poorly
nextGame.body:
If Rush were to play, Chicago's defense is built to beat exactly what he does. The Bears allow the 2nd-lowest EPA on short throws and the worst EPA in the league on deep throws. Rush almost never goes deep, with 5.34 intended air yards and two deep attempts all season. So he would be throwing into the strength of the coverage and ignoring its weakness. Chicago's sack rate ranks 7th, which tests a passer who has taken five sacks in 46 dropbacks.

Availability is the whole story here. Rush is the third quarterback, so he plays only if Penix (questionable, ribs, MRI scheduled) and the quarterback ahead of Rush both can't go. Penix's estimated return date is game day, which is a forecast, not a promise. On Chicago's side, Caleb Williams is out, and CB Kyler Gordon is out with Tyrique Stevenson questionable. That thins a secondary already leaking deep plays, which helps whoever starts for Atlanta more than it helps Rush. LB T.J. Edwards is questionable, which would matter for checkdowns to Bijan Robinson underneath.

keyMatchups.title: His short game vs Chicago's short defense
keyMatchups.body: Rush's offense runs through short throws and Robinson checkdowns, and Chicago gives up almost nothing there. With no deep shots to punish the Bears' worst area, his path to positive plays narrows to almost nothing.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush vs sack tendency
keyMatchups.body: Chicago gets home at a top-10 sack rate. Rush's season pressure-to-sack rate is alarming, though his career history says it should regress.

nextGame.watch: Penix's MRI result and practice status: only a double absence ahead of him puts Rush on the field.

restOfSeason.body: Expect little to nothing. He is QB3 on a team that would rather run, and any action likely comes in relief or a forced spot start. If he does start, the realistic outcome looks like his career norm, not this year's disaster. That means roughly 6 yards per attempt and modestly negative EPA, with interceptions remaining the main risk. The sack and interception rates should come down from their current extremes, while the below-expected accuracy and the short, sticks-averse passing are lasting traits.
swingFactors: Health of the quarterback ahead of him
Atlanta leaning on its run game in any Rush start

confidence.note: 46 dropbacks, and he's QB3 with no clear path to snaps.
